issue.title: Proposal: Nostr relay discovery via Namecoin (.bit hostnames) — N2
issue.body:
## Proposal — Nostr relay discovery via Namecoin (`wss://relay.example.bit`)

`RelayManagementCard` lets users add app-catalog relay URLs by hostname. Right now those hostnames resolve through DNS — fine for `relay.zapstore.dev`, but it means the *relay endpoint* itself is a DNS-revocable address. If `relay.zapstore.dev` is taken down or hijacked, an attacker who controls the hijacked DNS record can serve malicious catalog events.

This proposal adds support for adding relays addressed by a **Namecoin name** (`relay.example.bit` or `example.bit`). The hostname-to-`wss://` mapping comes from the on-chain Namecoin record, not DNS.

### Why this fits Zapstore's vision

- "Decentralized catalogs" — the docs already say "anyone can run a relay and publish their own app catalog." Adding `.bit` removes the last DNS dependency from that story.
- Defence-in-depth alongside the relay-pubkey-signed app events that Zapstore already uses (`kTrustedRelayPubkeys`): the *content* trust is already pubkey-anchored, this adds *transport* trust anchored in the same way.

### Spec

[mstrofnone/nips — N2](https://github.com/mstrofnone/nips/blob/master/N2.md)

Layers cleanly on top of the existing Namecoin record container ([ifa-0001](https://github.com/namecoin/proposals/blob/master/ifa-0001.md)). The same `nostr.relays` array used by NIP-65 outbox hints is reused — no new schema.

### What this would add to Zapstore

- A `NamecoinRelayResolver` that maps `wss://relay.example.bit` → an `nostr.relay` value from the on-chain record, plumbed into the existing relay-add flow in `RelayManagementCard`.
- Validation that the resolved value is a syntactically valid `wss://` URL before persisting.
- Settings toggle "Allow `.bit` relay hostnames", off by default.
- Tests covering: bare `.bit`, subdomain `.bit`, expired name, name-not-found, ElectrumX unreachable.

### Reference implementation

Production resolver code lives at [ethicnology/dart-nostr#44](https://github.com/ethicnology/dart-nostr/pull/44) (merged). Same module that backs the N1 proposal — the resolver is shared.

### Dependency on N1

This proposal **does not** require N1 to land first, but it can share the same `NamecoinResolverService` if both land. Independent issue/PR by design.

### Asking permission

Same as N1 — happy to draft a `spec/features/` packet first or open a feature-flagged draft PR. Let me know.

issue.title: Proposal: TLSA pinning for .bit relay WebSockets (RFC 6698) — N3
issue.body:
## Proposal — TLSA pinning for `.bit` Nostr relay WebSockets (RFC 6698)

Follow-up to the Namecoin relay discovery proposal (#365). If Zapstore is going to accept relay URLs whose hostname resolves via Namecoin (`relay.example.bit`), the matching TLS certificate should be pinned against an on-chain hash — otherwise the chain has authenticated the *hostname* but a CA-mis-issued cert could still MitM the WebSocket.

### Why this fits Zapstore's vision

- INVARIANTS: "APKs must never be installed unless their hash matches the expected value." Same principle, applied to the TLS session that delivers the release event in the first place.
- Sovereignty: pins move trust from "the public CA system did not lie to me today" to "this hash is in the chain I trust." Fits the broader anti-gatekeeper posture.

### Honest constraints (Flutter-specific)

Flutter's high-level `WebSocket` class does **not** expose the peer certificate. Implementing this honestly on Android needs one of:

- A platform channel to OkHttp's `CertificatePinner`, or
- A custom `IOClient` + `SecurityContext` configured per-connection.

**This proposal is therefore scoped as a two-stage delivery:**

1. **Stage 1 (this PR if greenlit):** Resolver-layer support — fetch and parse `tlsa` records from the Namecoin record container, expose them via the `NamecoinResolverService`, **gate the relay-add UI** to warn when a TLSA record exists but is not yet enforced. No enforcement code yet.

2. **Stage 2 (follow-up):** Platform-channel cert verification on Android. Tracked as a separate issue once Stage 1 lands.

This staging matches QUALITY_BAR ("happy-path-only implementations are insufficient" — but it also explicitly avoids shipping fake enforcement).

### Spec

[mstrofnone/nips — N3](https://github.com/mstrofnone/nips/blob/master/N3.md)

Re-uses the [ifa-0003](https://github.com/namecoin/proposals/blob/master/ifa-0003.md) "Dehydrated TLS Certificates" record shape. No new top-level keys.

### What Stage 1 would add to Zapstore

- TLSA record parser (already exists in dart-nostr#44).
- Visible "TLSA pin available, not yet enforced" badge on relay entries.
- Diagnostics-screen surface showing parsed pins for inspection.

### Asking permission

This one's the most architecturally invasive of the four (Stage 2 touches platform code). Even more reason to surface the proposal before any code. Will defer entirely if the team prefers to skip — Stage 1 alone is mostly diagnostic plumbing.

issue.title: Proposal: Service attestations (kind 38383/38384) — N4
issue.body:
## Proposal — Service attestations (kind 38383/38384) with optional Namecoin identity anchor

The trust model has three tiers: explicit allowlist → `zapstore.yaml` repo verification → Vertex social-graph reputation. Vertex is the soft underbelly — pure follower/PageRank reputation is gameable, and the docs already acknowledge "Nostr pubkeys are pseudonymous and cheap to generate."

This proposal would add a **fourth trust signal**: a portable, signed, queryable layer of *service attestations* — kind 38383 events where one pubkey says "this other pubkey did X service, and I rate it Y/Z." When the attestee's identity is anchored in Namecoin, the attestation can be re-verified at the on-chain block height the work was done — so reputation survives both attester and attestee rotating keys.

### Why this fits Zapstore's vision

- VISION: "users can reliably discover and install apps offline-first / installs and updates are verifiable and safe." A signed attestation is verifiable offline (cached event + chain proof at a fixed height).
- The "Verification on install" section of the trust model can grow a new optional line: *"developer has N independent service attestations at trust level T"* alongside the existing pubkey + APK-hash + cert-link checks.
- Doesn't replace Vertex — *complements* it. Both can feed into the same trust score.

### Spec

[mstrofnone/nips — N4](https://github.com/mstrofnone/nips/blob/master/N4.md)

Defines two parameterised-replaceable kinds:
- `38383` — single attestation (`p`, `service`, `rating`, optional `nmc` Namecoin anchor)
- `38384` — attester's curated "currently active" set

Both wire-compatible with NIP-32 labels.

### Status disclosure

This is the **least mature** of the four proposals — it is draft-only in the upstream NIP track, with no production implementation yet. **I do not propose shipping it as enforced trust in Zapstore until at least one independent implementation exists.** What I'd like to ship now is:

- A read-only ingest: `AttestationQueryService` that queries kind 38383 about developer pubkeys.
- A "trust signal" surface in `app_detail_screen` showing attester count + average rating, **clearly labelled experimental**.
- No effect on whitelisting, blocking, or install flow.

That way Zapstore can be a reference reader for the kind without taking on enforcement risk before the kind has rough consensus on `nostr-protocol/nips`.

### Asking permission

Of all four proposals, this is the one most worth saying "not yet" to. Posting it for completeness and discussion, not as a push. Comfortable parking this until the kind is more mature.

issue.title: Proposal: NIP-05 verification via Namecoin (.bit identifiers) — N1
issue.body:
## Proposal — NIP-05 verification via Namecoin (`.bit` identifiers)

Right now `ProfileIdentityRow` renders `profile.nip05` as a plain string with a check icon, but there is no verification step behind it (no DNS lookup, no `/.well-known/nostr.json` fetch, no signature/pubkey match check). That looks identical for a real NIP-05 and a self-claimed one.

This proposal adds *verified* NIP-05 support — and specifically supports identifiers anchored in the Namecoin blockchain (`alice@example.bit`, `example.bit`, `id/alice`) — without DNS or a CA in the trust path.

### Why this fits Zapstore's vision

- VISION.md: "users who value open networks and self-custody … without centralized app store control" — a verified `.bit` identifier removes DNS/CA as a takedown vector for the developer's own identity.
- INVARIANTS: "signed Nostr events must be verified before use" — extends that posture to the identity label rendered next to a developer.
- Trust model docs already lean on the developer's Nostr pubkey for whitelisting and install verification. A blockchain-anchored `nip05` gives a cheap, fully-decentralised second factor that the relay's Vertex tier can't game.

### Spec

Draft NIP, deliberately written to be implementable independently of other Namecoin NIPs:
[mstrofnone/nips — N1](https://github.com/mstrofnone/nips/blob/master/N1.md)

Wire-compatible with the Namecoin project's [ifa-0001](https://github.com/namecoin/proposals/blob/master/ifa-0001.md) record format and adds **zero new top-level keys** to the Namecoin record schema.

### What this would add to Zapstore

- A `NamecoinNip05Service` (Riverpod) that resolves `.bit`-suffixed `nip05` values via an ElectrumX-NMC WebSocket transport (browser/mobile-safe; no raw TCP needed).
- Verified / unverified / pending states surfaced on `ProfileIdentityRow` — explicit per QUALITY_BAR.
- Off by default behind a settings toggle "Verify `.bit` identities" so existing UX is untouched until the user opts in.
- Tests covering all four states (unset / verified / mismatch / unreachable) per QUALITY_BAR.

### Reference implementation

The resolver, TLSA helpers, and parser code already exist as a production-quality port at [ethicnology/dart-nostr#44](https://github.com/ethicnology/dart-nostr/pull/44) (merged), with 526/526 tests passing including live-blockchain smoke tests. We would adapt a trimmed subset into a self-contained `lib/services/namecoin/` module — no extra runtime deps, no purplebase changes.

### Asking permission, per CONTRIBUTING

Per the README ("please reach out to us first before working on any contribution!") I'm opening this as a proposal rather than a PR. Happy to:

1. Drop the proposal if it's not aligned, or
2. Draft a feature spec under `spec/features/` first, or
3. Open a draft PR with the resolver + UI behind a feature flag, ready for review.

Let me know which direction you'd prefer. PR follows immediately if option 3.

issue.title: feat(N4): service attestation (kind 38383) ingest — experimental, draft for #362
issue.body:
Draft PR for #362.

## What this does

Adds a **read-only ingest** path for NIP-N4 `kind:38383` service attestations:

* `ServiceAttestation` plain-Dart model
* Tolerant parser from `(attesterPubkey, createdAtSec, tags, content)` → model
* `dedupeAttestations()` — newest wins per `(attesterPubkey, dTag)`
* `AttestationSummary` — attester count, attestation count, average rating, Namecoin-anchored count
* `AttestationQueryService` — pulls `kind:38383` events from local storage and produces a summary
* `attestationSummaryProvider` Riverpod family for future UI consumption

## What this does *not* do — explicitly

Per the proposal in #362:

* **No UI surface.** No badge on the dev profile, no row on the app detail screen.
* **No influence on whitelisting / blocking / install.** Trust model is untouched.
* **No Namecoin anchor verification.** The `nmc` tag is parsed and counted but no chain query happens.

The proposal explicitly framed N4 as the one of the four most worth saying "not yet" to. This PR honours that — it lands the *reader* so the kind is ingestable when it stabilises, and otherwise has zero behavioural effect.

## Why ship anything at all?

Two reasons:

1. **Reference reader.** Having a working ingest path in a real Nostr app raises the bar for the kind to stabilise. The structural choices in the parser surface real questions about the NIP (e.g. should `rating` always be 0..1 normalised? what about `rating > max`?). Those questions can now be answered against running code, not slideware.
2. **Cheap to revert.** It is ~340 LOC of plain-Dart in a self-contained directory with no app-wide touch points. If N4 dies upstream, the directory deletes cleanly.

## Why draft

Same reason as #366 / #367 / #368 — per the README + spec-first workflow, this is for review not for merge. *Explicit invitation*: a "not now" close is a fine outcome. The proposal already disclosed N4 as least mature of the four.

## Architecture fit

- All new code under `lib/services/attestations/` — no app-wide touch.
- No `models` change. `ServiceAttestation` is plain Dart so this can ship without coordinated package releases.
- No `purplebase` change. Query uses the same `Request<Model<dynamic>>(...)` pattern that `deletion_processor.dart` already uses for ad-hoc kind queries.
- `LocalSource` only — service does not generate background network traffic when the feature is unused.

## What's in the diff

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `lib/services/attestations/attestation_models.dart` | `ServiceAttestation`, `AttestationSummary`, `NamecoinAttestationAnchor` |
| `lib/services/attestations/attestation_parser.dart` | Tolerant parser + `dedupeAttestations()` |
| `lib/services/attestations/attestation_query_service.dart` | Storage query + Riverpod provider |
| `spec/work/WORK-N4-service-attestations.md` | Work packet with experimental disclaimer |
| `test/services/attestations/attestation_parser_test.dart` | 18 tests covering parser, dedupe, summary |

## Verification

```
flutter pub get      → clean
flutter analyze      → No issues found! (full project)
flutter test         → 35/35 passing
```

Tested on Flutter 3.41.4 / Dart 3.11.1 (not 3.38.6 from `.fvmrc` — host doesn't have FVM, but the SDK constraints in pubspec.yaml are satisfied; flagging for awareness).

## Sibling proposals

- #366 — N1 PR: NIP-05 verification via Namecoin
- #367 — N2 PR: relay discovery via Namecoin
- #368 — N3 PR: TLSA pin parsing (Stage 1)

N4 is fully independent of those three; no shared code.

issue.title: feat(N3): Stage 1 TLSA pin parsing for .bit relays — draft for #364
issue.body:
Draft PR for #364.

## What this does — Stage 1 only

Adds RFC 6698 TLSA pin **parsing** for `.bit` relay hostnames. `NamecoinTlsaService` fetches the on-chain record, parses any `tls` entries, and returns them in a sealed-class state model:

* `NotApplicable` — host is not `.bit`
* `PinsAvailable` — pins were parsed; ready to be enforced (separately)
* `NoPins` — record exists but has no TLSA entries
* `Unknown` — name not registered / expired / record unparseable
* `Unreachable` — every configured ElectrumX server failed

**No connection-time enforcement is added by this PR.** That is Stage 2 (see below).

## Why Stage 1 is shipped alone

Flutter's high-level `WebSocket` API does not expose the peer certificate. Enforcing pins needs either an Android platform channel into OkHttp's `CertificatePinner` or a custom `IOClient`/`SecurityContext` pipeline. Either path is invasive enough to warrant its own design conversation.

Per `spec/guidelines/QUALITY_BAR.md`: "Happy-path-only implementations are insufficient" — but it would be much worse to ship fake enforcement. This PR's API is honest: it tells you a pin exists and what it pins, but doesn't pretend to enforce it.

Stage 2 can ship as a follow-up; the Stage 1 API is stable across that transition.

## Why draft

Same reason as #366 / #367 — per the README + spec-first workflow, this is for review not for merge. Particular invitation for review here: **is Stage 1 alone interesting to land?** If the answer is "no, we'd rather hold this until Stage 2 is ready," that is a fine outcome and I'll close.

Adds support for `wss://relay.example.bit` style relay URLs in `RelayManagementCard`. issue.body:
Draft PR for #363.

## What this does

Adds opt-in NIP-05 verification of `.bit` / `d/<name>` / `id/<name>` identifiers against the Namecoin blockchain, via an ElectrumX-NMC WebSocket transport (no raw TCP, no native deps, works on Flutter Android out of the box).

Today `ProfileIdentityRow` renders `profile.nip05` next to an unconditional check icon — there's no underlying verification step at all (no DNS resolution, no `.well-known/nostr.json` fetch, no signature/pubkey match). This PR adds verification for the `.bit` subset and surfaces the outcome in explicit per-state UI (verified / mismatch / unverified / unreachable / resolving / not-applicable).

DNS-based NIP-05 verification is **out of scope** — that is a separate gap and a separate conversation.

## Why draft

Per the README ("please reach out to us first") and the spec-first workflow in `spec/guidelines/QUALITY_BAR.md` ("behavior changes require a feature spec first"), this is staged as a draft for design review. Issue #363 is the proposal; this PR is the staging diff so you can see exactly what changes if it lands.

Happy to:
- Convert the work packet to a feature spec under `spec/features/` if preferred
- Move the badge placement / styling
- Pin the default ElectrumX server set to something Zapstore-controlled
- Or close this if it's not aligned

## Architecture fit

Per `spec/guidelines/ARCHITECTURE.md`:
- All new code lives under `lib/services/namecoin/` and `lib/widgets/common/` — UI-facing orchestration, not domain logic
- No `models` or `purplebase` change
- No relay-pool or storage touch
- `ProfileIdentityRow` is unchanged for non-`.bit` identifiers (no regression risk)

Per `spec/guidelines/INVARIANTS.md`:
- UI thread never blocks (async + `FutureProvider.autoDispose`)
- Every error maps to a sealed-class state — no silent failures
- Mismatched on-chain pubkeys are an *explicit* state, not a fall-through to "verified"
- Parser tolerates malformed/unknown/future fields (covered by tests)

## What's in the diff

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `lib/services/namecoin/electrumx_client.dart` | WebSocket transport (ported from dart-nostr#44, CC0) |
| `lib/services/namecoin/electrumx_server.dart` | Default server list |
| `lib/services/namecoin/script.dart` | Namecoin script parser |
| `lib/services/namecoin/value.dart` | NIP-N0 `nostr` field extractor |
| `lib/services/namecoin/identifier.dart` | `.bit` / `d/` / `id/` parser |
| `lib/services/namecoin/record_parser.dart` | Host-flat splitter, relay/tor walkers (TLSA deferred to N3) |
| `lib/services/namecoin/namecoin_nip05_service.dart` | Riverpod-friendly service with sealed-class state model |
| `lib/widgets/common/namecoin_nip05_badge.dart` | Replacement NIP-05 row with verification badge |
| `lib/widgets/common/profile_identity_row.dart` | One-line swap to use the new badge |
| `pubspec.yaml` | Promotes `crypto` and `convert` to direct deps (both were transitive) |
| `spec/work/WORK-N1-namecoin-nip05.md` | Work packet (per AGENTS.md) |
| `test/services/namecoin/record_parser_test.dart` | 18 parser tests |
| `test/services/namecoin/namecoin_nip05_service_test.dart` | 12 service tests across every sealed state |

## Verification

```
flutter pub get      → clean
flutter analyze      → No issues found! (full project)
flutter test         → 47/47 passing (30 new + 17 pre-existing)
```

Tested on Flutter 3.41.4 / Dart 3.11.1 (not 3.38.6 from `.fvmrc` — host doesn't have FVM, but the SDK constraints in pubspec.yaml are satisfied; flagging for awareness).

## Reference implementation

The transport, parser, and identifier code are ported verbatim (CC0) from [ethicnology/dart-nostr#44](https://github.com/ethicnology/dart-nostr/pull/44) (merged) — same code that backs the Amethyst Android / KMP iOS / Desktop ports and the strfry sidecar. 526/526 tests pass in the upstream against live blockchain.

- #365 — N2: relay discovery via Namecoin (`wss://relay.example.bit`). Reuses this module's resolver.
- #364 — N3: TLSA pinning for `.bit` relay WebSockets. Reuses the parser, adds an enforcement layer.
- #362 — N4: Service attestations (kind 38383/38384). Independent surface; experimental.

This PR is fully independent of those three — review and merge order is up to you.

issue.title: Proposal: Service attestations (kind 38383/38384) — N4
issue.body:
## Proposal — Service attestations (kind 38383/38384) with optional Namecoin identity anchor

The trust model has three tiers: explicit allowlist → `zapstore.yaml` repo verification → Vertex social-graph reputation. Vertex is the soft underbelly — pure follower/PageRank reputation is gameable, and the docs already acknowledge "Nostr pubkeys are pseudonymous and cheap to generate."

This proposal would add a **fourth trust signal**: a portable, signed, queryable layer of *service attestations* — kind 38383 events where one pubkey says "this other pubkey did X service, and I rate it Y/Z." When the attestee's identity is anchored in Namecoin, the attestation can be re-verified at the on-chain block height the work was done — so reputation survives both attester and attestee rotating keys.

### Why this fits Zapstore's vision

- VISION: "users can reliably discover and install apps offline-first / installs and updates are verifiable and safe." A signed attestation is verifiable offline (cached event + chain proof at a fixed height).
- The "Verification on install" section of the trust model can grow a new optional line: *"developer has N independent service attestations at trust level T"* alongside the existing pubkey + APK-hash + cert-link checks.
- Doesn't replace Vertex — *complements* it. Both can feed into the same trust score.

### Spec

[mstrofnone/nips — N4](https://github.com/mstrofnone/nips/blob/master/N4.md)

Defines two parameterised-replaceable kinds:
- `38383` — single attestation (`p`, `service`, `rating`, optional `nmc` Namecoin anchor)
- `38384` — attester's curated "currently active" set

Both wire-compatible with NIP-32 labels.

### Status disclosure

This is the **least mature** of the four proposals — it is draft-only in the upstream NIP track, with no production implementation yet. **I do not propose shipping it as enforced trust in Zapstore until at least one independent implementation exists.** What I'd like to ship now is:

- A read-only ingest: `AttestationQueryService` that queries kind 38383 about developer pubkeys.
- A "trust signal" surface in `app_detail_screen` showing attester count + average rating, **clearly labelled experimental**.
- No effect on whitelisting, blocking, or install flow.

That way Zapstore can be a reference reader for the kind without taking on enforcement risk before the kind has rough consensus on `nostr-protocol/nips`.

### Asking permission

Of all four proposals, this is the one most worth saying "not yet" to. Posting it for completeness and discussion, not as a push. Comfortable parking this until the kind is more mature.

issue.title: Proposal: Nostr relay discovery via Namecoin (.bit hostnames) — N2
issue.body:
## Proposal — Nostr relay discovery via Namecoin (`wss://relay.example.bit`)

`RelayManagementCard` lets users add app-catalog relay URLs by hostname. Right now those hostnames resolve through DNS — fine for `relay.zapstore.dev`, but it means the *relay endpoint* itself is a DNS-revocable address. If `relay.zapstore.dev` is taken down or hijacked, an attacker who controls the hijacked DNS record can serve malicious catalog events.

This proposal adds support for adding relays addressed by a **Namecoin name** (`relay.example.bit` or `example.bit`). The hostname-to-`wss://` mapping comes from the on-chain Namecoin record, not DNS.

### Why this fits Zapstore's vision

- "Decentralized catalogs" — the docs already say "anyone can run a relay and publish their own app catalog." Adding `.bit` removes the last DNS dependency from that story.
- Defence-in-depth alongside the relay-pubkey-signed app events that Zapstore already uses (`kTrustedRelayPubkeys`): the *content* trust is already pubkey-anchored, this adds *transport* trust anchored in the same way.

### Spec

[mstrofnone/nips — N2](https://github.com/mstrofnone/nips/blob/master/N2.md)

Layers cleanly on top of the existing Namecoin record container ([ifa-0001](https://github.com/namecoin/proposals/blob/master/ifa-0001.md)). The same `nostr.relays` array used by NIP-65 outbox hints is reused — no new schema.

### What this would add to Zapstore

- A `NamecoinRelayResolver` that maps `wss://relay.example.bit` → an `nostr.relay` value from the on-chain record, plumbed into the existing relay-add flow in `RelayManagementCard`.
- Validation that the resolved value is a syntactically valid `wss://` URL before persisting.
- Settings toggle "Allow `.bit` relay hostnames", off by default.
- Tests covering: bare `.bit`, subdomain `.bit`, expired name, name-not-found, ElectrumX unreachable.

### Reference implementation

Production resolver code lives at [ethicnology/dart-nostr#44](https://github.com/ethicnology/dart-nostr/pull/44) (merged). Same module that backs the N1 proposal — the resolver is shared.

### Dependency on N1

This proposal **does not** require N1 to land first, but it can share the same `NamecoinResolverService` if both land. Independent issue/PR by design.

### Asking permission

Same as N1 — happy to draft a `spec/features/` packet first or open a feature-flagged draft PR. Let me know.

issue.title: Proposal: NIP-05 verification via Namecoin (.bit identifiers) — N1
issue.body:
## Proposal — NIP-05 verification via Namecoin (`.bit` identifiers)

Right now `ProfileIdentityRow` renders `profile.nip05` as a plain string with a check icon, but there is no verification step behind it (no DNS lookup, no `/.well-known/nostr.json` fetch, no signature/pubkey match check). That looks identical for a real NIP-05 and a self-claimed one.

This proposal adds *verified* NIP-05 support — and specifically supports identifiers anchored in the Namecoin blockchain (`alice@example.bit`, `example.bit`, `id/alice`) — without DNS or a CA in the trust path.

### Why this fits Zapstore's vision

- VISION.md: "users who value open networks and self-custody … without centralized app store control" — a verified `.bit` identifier removes DNS/CA as a takedown vector for the developer's own identity.
- INVARIANTS: "signed Nostr events must be verified before use" — extends that posture to the identity label rendered next to a developer.
- Trust model docs already lean on the developer's Nostr pubkey for whitelisting and install verification. A blockchain-anchored `nip05` gives a cheap, fully-decentralised second factor that the relay's Vertex tier can't game.

### Spec

Draft NIP, deliberately written to be implementable independently of other Namecoin NIPs:
[mstrofnone/nips — N1](https://github.com/mstrofnone/nips/blob/master/N1.md)

Wire-compatible with the Namecoin project's [ifa-0001](https://github.com/namecoin/proposals/blob/master/ifa-0001.md) record format and adds **zero new top-level keys** to the Namecoin record schema.

### What this would add to Zapstore

- A `NamecoinNip05Service` (Riverpod) that resolves `.bit`-suffixed `nip05` values via an ElectrumX-NMC WebSocket transport (browser/mobile-safe; no raw TCP needed).
- Verified / unverified / pending states surfaced on `ProfileIdentityRow` — explicit per QUALITY_BAR.
- Off by default behind a settings toggle "Verify `.bit` identities" so existing UX is untouched until the user opts in.
- Tests covering all four states (unset / verified / mismatch / unreachable) per QUALITY_BAR.

### Reference implementation

The resolver, TLSA helpers, and parser code already exist as a production-quality port at [ethicnology/dart-nostr#44](https://github.com/ethicnology/dart-nostr/pull/44) (merged), with 526/526 tests passing including live-blockchain smoke tests. We would adapt a trimmed subset into a self-contained `lib/services/namecoin/` module — no extra runtime deps, no purplebase changes.

### Asking permission, per CONTRIBUTING

Per the README ("please reach out to us first before working on any contribution!") I'm opening this as a proposal rather than a PR. Happy to:

1. Drop the proposal if it's not aligned, or
2. Draft a feature spec under `spec/features/` first, or
3. Open a draft PR with the resolver + UI behind a feature flag, ready for review.

Let me know which direction you'd prefer. PR follows immediately if option 3.

issue.title: Proposal: TLSA pinning for .bit relay WebSockets (RFC 6698) — N3
issue.body:
## Proposal — TLSA pinning for `.bit` Nostr relay WebSockets (RFC 6698)

Follow-up to the Namecoin relay discovery proposal (#365). If Zapstore is going to accept relay URLs whose hostname resolves via Namecoin (`relay.example.bit`), the matching TLS certificate should be pinned against an on-chain hash — otherwise the chain has authenticated the *hostname* but a CA-mis-issued cert could still MitM the WebSocket.

### Why this fits Zapstore's vision

- INVARIANTS: "APKs must never be installed unless their hash matches the expected value." Same principle, applied to the TLS session that delivers the release event in the first place.
- Sovereignty: pins move trust from "the public CA system did not lie to me today" to "this hash is in the chain I trust." Fits the broader anti-gatekeeper posture.

### Honest constraints (Flutter-specific)

Flutter's high-level `WebSocket` class does **not** expose the peer certificate. Implementing this honestly on Android needs one of:

- A platform channel to OkHttp's `CertificatePinner`, or
- A custom `IOClient` + `SecurityContext` configured per-connection.

**This proposal is therefore scoped as a two-stage delivery:**

1. **Stage 1 (this PR if greenlit):** Resolver-layer support — fetch and parse `tlsa` records from the Namecoin record container, expose them via the `NamecoinResolverService`, **gate the relay-add UI** to warn when a TLSA record exists but is not yet enforced. No enforcement code yet.

2. **Stage 2 (follow-up):** Platform-channel cert verification on Android. Tracked as a separate issue once Stage 1 lands.

This staging matches QUALITY_BAR ("happy-path-only implementations are insufficient" — but it also explicitly avoids shipping fake enforcement).

### Spec

[mstrofnone/nips — N3](https://github.com/mstrofnone/nips/blob/master/N3.md)

Re-uses the [ifa-0003](https://github.com/namecoin/proposals/blob/master/ifa-0003.md) "Dehydrated TLS Certificates" record shape. No new top-level keys.

### What Stage 1 would add to Zapstore

- TLSA record parser (already exists in dart-nostr#44).
- Visible "TLSA pin available, not yet enforced" badge on relay entries.
- Diagnostics-screen surface showing parsed pins for inspection.

### Asking permission

This one's the most architecturally invasive of the four (Stage 2 touches platform code). Even more reason to surface the proposal before any code. Will defer entirely if the team prefers to skip — Stage 1 alone is mostly diagnostic plumbing.
